hook: A molybdenum enzyme passes sulfur over 50 angstroms along a persulfide relay to make ergothioneine.

readout.label: Sulfur transfer distance between active sites

summary: Using cryo-EM, crystallography and spectroscopy, the team showed how a bacterial enzyme pulls sulfur from cysteine and relays it to a molybdenum center to attach it to a histidine derivative. The reaction is reversible, hinting ergothioneine stores oxidizing power. Findings come from one enzyme in one bacterium, and the metabolic role is inferred.
title: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
